slides.title: Two halves of security
slides.text: Physical security protects the machine: a locked door, a cable lock. Digital security protects the data: a passphrase, two-step sign-in, a firewall.
slides.alt: Physical or digital: a cable lock and a privacy screen are physical; encryption and a virus scanner are digital.

slides.title: The padlock
slides.text: HTTPS shows as a padlock. Your details travel in a sealed envelope instead of an open postcard. It seals the trip; it does not make the shop honest.
slides.alt: The shop order rides the padlock street: sealed roads wear padlocks, while the open street is shorter but read by a snoopy cat.

slides.title: Strong passphrases
slides.text: Four random words beat a short word with a number added. Use a different one for each account, so one leak cannot open everything.
slides.alt: Four random word tiles make the key: volcano, giraffe, bicycle, thunder. A computer would need about centuries.

slides.title: Think before you post
slides.text: Making something public has a benefit and a risk. Posting where you will be helps friends find you, and it tells strangers too.
slides.alt: Share or Shield: where you live. Good side: friends could send you a card. Risk: a stranger could turn up at your door.

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Packet Post at Lock It and finish all 7 levels. In the game your passphrase is called your mailbox key. For each choice, name the benefit and the risk.
